result.rationale: The migration inserts legacy setting values verbatim (`INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) without normalization, while `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)` — an exact match against the referer's hostname. A legacy value like 'http://discourse.org' (or 'https://example.com/1234', which even appears in the spec as a fabricated host) would never equal 'discourse.org', whereas the removed `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` stripped schemes/paths. So migrated entries silently fail to authorize embedding.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration copies legacy SiteSetting 'embeddable_hosts' lines directly into the embeddable_hosts table via raw SQL (execute "INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"). This bypasses EmbeddableHost's before_validation normalization that strips scheme and paths (app/models/embeddable_host.rb). Later, host checks use EmbeddableHost.record_for_host/host_allowed? which parse the referer URL to uri.host and compare against stored host (where("lower(host) = ?", host)). If migrated rows contain values like "https://example.com/1234" (as allowed by the old setting format), they will be stored unnormalized and won't match uri.host ("example.com"), breaking embedding for migrated installs.
